messages:
sara: Heads-up — we have a canary problem. fnhook payloads from slice s-117 are arriving at tools with PII keys stripped by the validator, and the downstream enrichment tool fails with 422 because it expects contact.email. Customer reported 3 failures in last 15m.

mike: Which validator did we flip last night? schema-gate or the fncall binding one? :thinking_face:

sara: The strict_fncall gate (rolled at 02:10 UTC). Canary ~10% (s-117). Example incoming body we received (trimmed):
```json
{"user_id":"u_123","contact":{ /* email missing here */ },"metadata":{"note":"..."}}
```
The original model output included `contact.email` but validator removed it because of extra/unknown property rules on the binding.

evan: If validator is stripping fields that sounds like `remove_unknown=true` behavior. That was intentional for sync QoS to avoid hard rejects, but silent drop for PII-sensitive keys is bad. Should have emitted a warning header at minimum.

leo: Customer side: their tool expects `contact.email` (used to hash/normalize). When missing tool returns 422 and we mark the fnhook as failed. They prefer a warning + fallback to hashed id rather than a silent drop.

sara: Current strict gate default is coercion (drop unknown props) to keep high availability. We thought failing fast would break too many older integrations. Guessing that design tradeoff backfired here.

mike: Telemetry — seeing spike in `hook.parse.partial` and `toolhook.fail.422` for s-117. Dashboard link: https://console/redwood/dashboards/eng/fnhook-parse?slice=s-117 (private). Ops bot just fired ~12 alerts in 20m.

ops-bot: Alert: 12 incidents in last 20m for fnhook parsing errors (slice s-117). Severity: P2. Related metric: validation.drop_count increased x120.

evan: Proposal: change canary behavior to emit a structured warning and sample the dropped keys + hashed values instead of stripping silently. Longer term: add an explicit `strict_reject` mode for bindings that declare `deny_unknown=true`. Implementation notes:
- runtime: when `deny_unknown=true` -> return 400/422 (reject) OR return payload with `X-Validation-Warn: dropped_keys=email,phone` depending on feature flag.
- telemetry: add counters `validation.drop_count` and `validation.reject_count` tagged by route/model/route_id.
- console: surface last N dropped keys and counts for each route.

leo: UX + product: We need a rollout that avoids breaking customers. Suggested path: 1) revert strict gate on s-117 to restore prior behavior; 2) push a non-breaking warning header + telemetry for all routes for 48h; 3) provide a console flag to opt-in to strict reject with a grace period and migration docs. Also need quotas/charge implications documented (rejects vs dropped payloads).

mike: I can add new tiles for `validation.drop_count` and `validation.reject_count` with route filters. Also add an alert when drop_count > threshold in last 5m.

sara: Quick mitigation: I'll revert the strict gate back to s-0 for s-117 now. Then we add the warning header as a patch (no reject) within 24-48h. Longer fix: remote config toggle `fncall.strict.reject` and a 1-week grace period when turned on.

evan: Implementation detail: we should hash PII fields before storing any sampled payloads. Add `privacy_tag` on fields and only store hashed samples. Will route to security review.

ops-bot: Action created: ISSUE-2134 - revert strict gate on s-117 (assignee: sara). ISSUE-2135 - add validation telemetry + warning header (assignee: mike).

mike: I'll update the dashboard and add alerting. Also add a small console indicator: `Validation warnings: active` with a link to sampling logs.

sara: I'll draft console copy for the UX explaining what "Validation warnings" means and how to opt into strict rejects. Will also coordinate release notes.

leo: SGTM. One more ask: show the last 100 dropped keys in console but with hashed values and an explicit consent checkbox in the route settings to allow storing samples.

evan: +1 on consent piece. Security to sign off on hashed-sampling.

sara: Thanks all — rolling back now and filing follow-ups. :thumbsup:
